evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Not present. Rep jumped directly into confirming details (moving date, address, square footage) with no upfront framing about call duration, dependable quote, or waiting for customer agreement.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after extensive probing: 'do you have like any, any concerns about this move or any any any questions that you want answers to on this call' — this came only after Section 3 logistics walkthrough was complete, not before.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer said 'like the mirror of broken' but only one follow-up question paraphrased the concern; no genuine 'tell me more about that' dig. Rep pivoted to delivering the Two Promises instead of layering deeper.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Partial reflection: 'So what I'm hearing is just to make sure your main you want the mirrors to make sure to get, get pat in, in the furniture, right?' — reflects back one concern, but doesn't summarize all concerns raised or ask for confirmation that the list is complete.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full. Rep provided range: 'it's good to budget around $6,076 to $6,844' and personalized it to their two-day split scenario based on inventory and out-of-town distance.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full. Trip fee ($864), tri fee ($110 return), overnight fee ($240), 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, and 'no hidden fees' all disclosed upfront. Hourly rate ($96/mover, weekday) and coverage (supplies, taxes, insurance, truck, gas, reassembly) clearly framed.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. After the estimate delivery, rep asked 'Does that all seem fair to you? Do you have any questions?' but immediately continued talking without waiting for a genuine pause — customer responded 'Oh, no, I have no questions that is outside of my budget' without silence being held.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full. 'When we book your move we'll lock in a firm arrival window for you and if you're late, $50 comes off immediately then after the first hour it's an extra $25 for every thirty minutes after that.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full. 'No worries damage coverage. Up to $2,000 included. And we pay it out on in four to six days.'
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False. Rep did not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent after delivering the Two Promises. Customer raised mirror concern, rep delivered damage coverage framing, but no explicit close-out question confirming the concern was addressed.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. After customer said the estimate was outside budget, rep pivoted to explaining the two-day split and deposit-free booking. No genuine 'What's still concerning you?' follow-up.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: False. No version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' was asked.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never. Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' — when customer said the quote was outside budget, rep moved directly to 'I'll be sending everything to your email' and closed without an explicit ask.

top_strength: Danah conducted a thorough phone-based room-by-room inventory walkthrough, capturing detailed furniture and item counts across all spaces, and correctly offered the virtual walkthrough option upfront when the 2,400 sq ft home qualified for it.
coaching_note: Open every call with the quid pro quo framing (10–15 minute call + dependable quote you can depend on + explicit wait for yes) before diving into discovery — this call skipped it entirely and that loss of structure compounds throughout.
booking_note: Customer declined to book, stating the estimate was 'outside of my budget' and said 'I'm just gonna take the quote and kind of look at my other options.'
